rule.cn.title: Year-end bonus tax
rule.cn.lede: Tax on a one-time annual bonus taxed on its own, under announcement 2023 No. 30. In force to 31 Dec 2027.
rule.cn.works: Yes: the row, the rate and the deduction
rule.cn.p1: Divide the bonus by 12. That monthly figure picks a rate and a quick deduction from the table.
rule.cn.p2: Tax is the whole bonus times that rate, less the quick deduction, rounded down to the fen.
rule.cn.p3: This is the separate-taxation option. You may instead add the bonus to your yearly income; this rule does not model that.
rule.cn.sourceLong: Source: MOF and STA announcement 2023 No. 30, 18 Aug 2023, in force to 31 Dec 2027. Read from gov.cn on 21 Nov 2026.
rule.cn.tableHint: Monthly figure in yuan, from the announcement
rule.cn.how: Amounts are in fen. Comparing the bonus with 12 times each limit is the same as dividing by 12, so the circuit never divides by 12.
rule.cn.trapTitle: Six places where more bonus keeps less
rule.cn.trapBody: Just above each limit the whole bonus moves to the higher rate. A bonus a little over these amounts (yuan) keeps less than one exactly at them:
rule.cn.rounding: Down to the fen · our reading
rule.ng.title: Pay tax (PAYE)
rule.ng.lede: Annual tax on employment income under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, with rent relief and the minimum wage exemption.
rule.ng.source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025: s.30, s.58, Fourth Schedule
rule.ng.gives: Annual tax and a monthly twelfth
rule.ng.works: Yes: reliefs and the income in each band
rule.ng.p1: Take the year's gross pay. Subtract pension, NHF, NHIS, life insurance, mortgage interest and rent relief (a fifth of rent, at most ₦500,000).
rule.ng.p2: Tax what is left in bands: the first ₦800,000 at 0%, then 15%, 18%, 21%, 23% and 25%. Round down to the naira once, on the year.
rule.ng.p3: Gross pay at or below the minimum wage (₦840,000 a year) pays no tax at all.
rule.ng.sourceLong: Source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7), sections 30, 58 and 162 and the Fourth Schedule, read from the National Assembly copy on 21 Nov 2026.
rule.ng.tableHint: Taxable income for the year in naira, Fourth Schedule
rule.ng.how: All amounts are whole naira for the year. Tax is worked out in kobo exactly and rounded down once at the end.
rule.ng.trapTitle: One cliff just above the minimum wage
rule.ng.trapBody: With no deductions, {edge} a year pays nothing, while {from} pays {tax}. A raise of ₦1 lowers take-home pay by {loss}.
rule.ng.trapAfter: Worked out by hand from our reading. The trap finder will confirm it from the circuit alone.
rule.ng.minWage: Annual gross up to ₦840,000 · monthly test not settled
rule.ng.rounding: Down to the naira once a year · the Act is silent
rule.ng.monthly: A flat twelfth · employers work cumulatively
rule.sp.title: Pool split
rule.sp.lede: Our own rule for sharing a pot between share holders: 85% goes to holders in proportion to their shares, read at a fixed block.
rule.sp.gives: Whether a payout is the exact share, to the unit
rule.sp.works: Yes: the exact share next to the payout
rule.sp.funds: Not yet. Vault comes after the proofs
rule.sp.p1: Holders share 85% of the pot. A holder with shares out of total is owed pot × 85% × shares ÷ total.
rule.sp.p2: The payout is that amount rounded down to the unit (0.01 token). Whatever is rounded away stays in the vault.
rule.sp.p3: The circuit does not divide. It checks a claimed payout: it passes only if the payout is exactly that rounded-down share.
rule.sp.sourceLong: Source: our own rule, written 19 Nov 2026. Shares are read at a block fixed when a round opens.
rule.sp.how: Four 32-bit inputs: pot, shares, total and the claimed payout. The check compares two products, so no division is needed.
rule.sp.trapBody: More shares should never pay less, and the payouts can never add up to more than the holders' part of the pot.
rule.sp.trapAfter: Earlier models were checked in P0. On the circuit on X Layer these facts are not run yet.
rule.sp.vault: Not yet · the vault comes after the proofs

proof.title: Proofs
proof.lede: Every result the solvers gave on the circuits read from X Layer: what holds, what fails, and what no tool could decide within {minutes} minutes. Each result names the block it read.
proof.legendHolds2: Two tools each showed that no input breaks the fact.
proof.legendHolds1: One tool showed it. A second tool has not confirmed it yet.
proof.legendFails: A tool found an input that breaks it. That input was run on X Layer before it was recorded.
proof.legendUndecided: No tool answered within {minutes} minutes. It is neither proved nor broken.
proof.legendMutant: Broken copy: each fact is also asked of a copy of the rule with one deliberate error. The tools must find that error, or the result does not count.
proof.mutantNone: Not needed: the rule itself breaks it
proof.trapTitle: Where a bigger amount keeps less
proof.trapCn: Every bonus in a range keeps less than the amount just below the range does.
proof.trapNg: With no deductions, every gross pay in this range keeps less than {edge} does.
proof.trapHow: Found from the circuit alone by the trap finder: {queries} solver queries, {seconds} s, circuit read at block {block}. Each figure above was then run with eval on X Layer.
proof.trapMatch: Compared afterwards with {source}: the same ranges.
proof.trapComplete: The last query proved that no other range exists.
proof.trapIncomplete: The last query, "is any other range left?", got no answer within {minutes} minutes. These ranges are real; that there are no others is not proved.
proof.onChain: Asked of circuits {circuits}, as read from X Layer.
proof.onChainSplit: Each fact is proved on the rule's arithmetic by two solvers. A chain of checks then shows that circuit 8 on X Layer computes exactly that arithmetic (circuits {circuits}).
proof.chainBody: Each link was checked on the bytes read at block {block}, and each link's broken copy was caught.
proof.link1: The rule joined from modules equals the rule as written
proof.link2: Each module on X Layer equals its source, the 32 by 32 multiplier included
proof.link3: Circuit 8 with its modules equals the joined rule
proof.sup.one-payout-accepted: A holder has only one accepted payout
proof.sup.a-payout-accepted: Every valid holder has an accepted payout
proof.sup.no-overflow: No step of the check overflows
proof.repeatBody: Each result's file holds the question asked, the exact command and the solver's output. The method and every run are written up in the repository.
proof.engLede: A payroll engine is taped out on X Layer next to the rule, and the tools ask whether the two can ever give a different tax or take-home. The engines here are simulated: the Payproof team wrote them to show the check. They are not any vendor's code.
proof.engAt: At a bonus of {bonus}, the rule's tax is {ref} and the engine's is {eng}. Both were run with eval on X Layer.
proof.engMutant: Broken copy: the engine's tax raised by 0.01 at one bonus. The tools must see the change.
proof.engNote: A difference says only that the two circuits disagree for a valid input. It does not say which one reads the rule right.

splits.title: Splits
splits.lede: A split pays holders of a share token from a pot, round by round. Each payout is checked by the split-v1 circuit on X Layer, and nobody can change the rule or the circuits after the split is made.
splits.none: No split has been made yet.
splits.noRounds: No round has been opened yet.
payout.title: Check my payout
payout.lede: Enter an address to see, for each round, the shares it held when the round opened, what the rule gives for them and what it was paid. No sign-in needed.
payout.badAddress: An address is 0x followed by 40 letters and digits.
payout.claiming: Claiming: confirm in your wallet, then wait for X Layer…
payout.how: The rule gives each holder 85% of the pot times their shares over all shares, rounded down. The vault pays a claim only if circuit 8 on X Layer accepts that exact amount, so a claim that went through was paid what the rule gives. Shares are counted at the block before the round opened; moving shares later does not change that round.
eng.title: Engines
eng.lede: An engine is someone's own version of a rule, put up with a bounty. Anyone who finds an input where the engine and the rule give different answers can claim the bounty. The engines listed here are simulated: we built them to show how this works.
eng.how: A disproof is checked on X Layer: Listings runs the rule's circuit and the engine's circuit on the input and pays the bounty only if their answers differ.
hunt.title: Hunt listing {id}
hunt.lede: Try bonuses to see the rule's answer next to the engine's. Both circuits are read from X Layer and run in this page, so trying costs nothing and nothing is sent.
hunt.unsupported: This page can run engines listed against the China bonus rule only.
hunt.differ: They differ at this bonus. This input disproves the engine.
hunt.local: The search runs on this device, one fen at a time.
hunt.submitBody: Two transactions from your wallet. The first records a sealed commitment tied to your address, so nobody can copy your input and claim first. The second, in a later block, shows the input; Listings runs both circuits on it and pays you if they differ. A small secret for the second step is kept on this device until it is sent.
hunt.committing: Step 1 of 2: confirm the commitment in your wallet…
hunt.waiting: Step 2 of 2: waiting for the next block, then confirm the reveal in your wallet…
run.title: Run a split
run.lede: Open a round to pay a split's holders from a deposit, or make a new split. Both are sent from your own wallet.
run.depositHint: From this deposit alone, the fee circuit takes {fee} {sym} for the operator and holders share up to {holders} {sym}. The other {rest} {sym}, and whatever rounding down leaves, waits in the vault for the next round.
run.warn: Nobody can take a deposit back out, including us. Holders claim it through the circuits the split pinned. If one of those circuits stopped working for good, the deposit would stay in the vault.
run.approving: Allowing the vault to take the deposit: confirm in your wallet…
run.opening: Opening the round: confirm in your wallet…
run.notOperator: Anyone may open a round on any split; the fee still goes to the split's operator.
run.createBody: The split uses rule split-v1 (circuit 8), the 10% fee circuit {fee} and the parts {refs}. Their netlist hashes are pinned when the split is made.
run.shareHint: It must keep each holder's balance history (our reference share token does).
run.creating: Making the split: confirm in your wallet…
